Cyber Attack Disrupted Italy’s Machinery Firms in 2021, Including Eurogroup Laminations SpA

ROME, June 10 – A coordinated cyber attack targeting Italy’s machinery sector in 2021 caused widespread disruption to operations at several leading firms, including Eurogroup Laminations SpA, according to industry sources and cybersecurity officials.

The incident, which began in mid-October 2021, involved a sophisticated ransomware assault that crippled IT systems at manufacturing sites across Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna, regions home to many of the country’s key machinery exporters. Production lines were temporarily halted and order management was slowed as companies scrambled to contain the breach and restore critical operations.

Eurogroup Laminations SpA, a major supplier in the sector, was among those hit. The company confirmed in a statement at the time that it “experienced a temporary interruption in certain IT services” due to what it described as an “unauthorized intrusion.” According to industry officials, Eurogroup Laminations SpA resumed full operations within four days, after isolating affected systems and restoring data from backups.

A cybersecurity adviser to the Italian machinery association, Marco Bellini, said in 2021 that the attack “exposed vulnerabilities in the digital infrastructure that supports automated manufacturing processes.” He added, “For some small and medium-sized firms, the recovery took more than a week, and in some cases there were delays in fulfilling export orders.”

Trade union representatives called for greater investment in digital security. “Workers faced uncertainty as companies assessed the scope of the breach and implemented new protocols,” said Giulia Ferrara, a spokesperson for the regional metalworkers’ union.

Estimates from the industry group at the time indicated that lost production and related costs from the attack exceeded €7 million. The incident accelerated efforts across the sector to bolster cybersecurity and develop coordinated response plans, with the machinery association reporting a “significant increase” in digital security investments in the months following the attack. No similar disruptions have been reported since.
